{"id":"mimid-bcji","title":"spec: the MIMI binding does not specify the VTC call mapping that mimid already implements","description":"Mark asked 2026-11-23 whether any spec and implementation work had been
done on VTC endpoints being pushed around by MIMI. Checked: the code
exists and the binding spec does not describe it.

IMPLEMENTED IN MIMID, both directions:
- Inbound (project.rs:202-210): a received mimi-content part of
  disposition `session` whose URL is `https` or `wss` becomes a JMAP
  MessageAction of type `urn:ietf:params:jmap:chat:cap:vtc`, with the
  part's description as the action's `label`. Any other URL becomes a
  line of `body` instead. A `session` part is never fetched.
- Outbound (backend.rs:872-893): a `Message/set` create carrying one
  such action is sent as the mimi-content §5.10 ExternalPart, with a
  guard refusing anything else: "only a call ({VTC}) is sent over MIMI".

SPECIFIED:
- draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00 line 390 defines the action type itself:
  "`urn:ietf:params:jmap:chat:cap:vtc` -- video/voice teleconference.
  `uri` is a signaling or room URL (e.g., a WebRTC signaling endpoint, a
  Jitsi room URL, a SIP URI)."
- draft-atwood-jmap-vtc-00 (2394 lines) and draft-atwood-jmap-vtc-wss-00
  (711 lines) specify VTC itself.

NOT SPECIFIED, and this is the gap: draft-atwood-jmap-chat-mimi-00, the
binding that says how JMAP Chat maps onto MIMI, says nothing about it.
Grepped for `disposition`, `ExternalPart`, `MessageAction` and `5.10`:
the only ExternalPart text is about ATTACHMENTS (`assetUrl`,
`proxyDownload`, `assetLifetimeSecs`). There is no mention of the
`session` disposition and no mapping from a MIMI part to a MessageAction.
(The `session` hits on a plain grep are the JMAP Session object, a
different sense of the word -- checked, not the disposition.)

SO: mimid's behaviour is ahead of its specification. Another
implementation receiving a call invite from mimid has nothing to read
that tells it the part is a call endpoint, and one sending us a call has
no stated way to shape it. That is an interop hazard of exactly the kind
the interop day would hit: a call invite would arrive as an attachment
or as body text, and the user would see a bare URL or "unsupported
content".

PROPOSED, for Mark: add a section to draft-atwood-jmap-chat-mimi-00
beside §Reactions and §Topics -- call it Calls or Session Parts -- saying
what the code already does:
- a mimi-content part of disposition `session` maps to a MessageAction
  of type urn:ietf:params:jmap:chat:cap:vtc, `uri` from the part's URL
  and `label` from its description;
- the mapping holds in both directions, and such a part is never
  fetched, since the URL is a live endpoint rather than content;
- which URL schemes map (mimid takes https and wss, and puts anything
  else in the body) and what a receiver does with a scheme it does not
  support;
- that a converting party sends no other MessageAction type over MIMI,
  which is what mimid's guard enforces.

Editing the draft is a write to ~/PROJECT/jmap-chat-spec and needs
Mark's approval per write. Nothing posted.","status":"open","priority":2,"issue_type":"task","owner":"mark@reviewcommit.com","created_at":"2026-11-23T18:10:07.348151097Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","updated_at":"2026-11-23T18:10:07.348151097Z","labels":["human"]}

{"notes":"CORRECTED 2026-11-23: mimi-content DOES specify this, weakly and
deliberately. §5.10 "Conferencing" names the case, the `session`
disposition is IANA-registered as "a description of a multimedia
session, or URI used to join one", and there is a complete worked CBOR
example of a join-URL ExternalPart. §5.10 then says "Further discussion
of calling and conferencing functionality is out-of-scope of this
document", and everything in it is "could" rather than MUST or SHOULD.

That makes our own binding draft's silence a smaller gap than this bead
first said, and easier to fill: mimid is implementing §5.10's own
suggestion that a session part "could be processed differently by the
client (for example, alerting the user or presenting a dialog box)", and
the never-fetch rule has implicit support in §5.10's example, which
nulls expires, size, encAlg and hashAlg.

So the section to add to draft-atwood-jmap-chat-mimi-00 is a MAPPING,
citing §5.10, not an invention:
- a mimi-content part of disposition `session` maps to a MessageAction
  of type urn:ietf:params:jmap:chat:cap:vtc, `uri` from the part's url
  and `label` from its description, both directions;
- such a part is not fetched: it is an endpoint to act on, as §5.10's
  example implies by nulling every content-fetch field;
- which URL schemes map. mimid takes https and wss and puts anything
  else in the body. Worth stating as mimid's choice rather than a
  requirement, since §5.10 constrains nothing;
- ONE THING MIMID DOES NOT HANDLE and the draft should admit: the
  disposition's definition has two halves, "a description of a
  multimedia session, OR a URI used to join one". mimid handles only the
  URI. A description form -- SDP or similar -- is not converted at all.
  That is a real limitation to write down rather than leave to a reader
  to discover."}
